chunks.arabic_text: عَنِ الْأَبِ، عَنْ عَلِيٍّ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَيْمُونَ، عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ، عَنْ آبَائِهِ، عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ

translations.en: From his father, from Ali, from his father, from Ibn Maymun, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ: فَضْلُ الْعِلْمِ أَحَبُّ إِلَى اللَّهِ مِنْ فَضْلِ الْعِبَادَةِ وَأَفْضَلُ دِينِكُمُ الْوَرَعُ

translations.en: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The merit of knowledge is more beloved to Allah than the merit of worship, and the best of your religion is self-restraint (from sins).

en.summary: This hadith emphasizes the superiority of knowledge over mere ritual worship in the sight of Allah. It concludes by defining the essence of religious excellence as 'war'' (self-restraint or piety), highlighting that true faith is characterized by guarding oneself against sin.
en.seo_question: What is considered the best aspect of religion according to this hadith?
